summary:
ORBITAL COMMAND AI is an interactive, 3D space mission design and simulation platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

The project aims to make space mission planning more engaging, accessible, and understandable by providing an immersive mission-control environment where users can explore spacecraft, visualize rockets, and experience simulated launch sequences.

Inspired by the real-world challenges of designing space missions, the platform brings together mission information, interactive dashboards, 3D rocket visualization, space environments, and animated launch experiences in one interface.

Users can explore a space-themed environment, interact with mission-control elements, visualize spacecraft, and experience the different stages of a simulated rocket launch.

Our goal is to transform complex space mission concepts into an engaging interactive experience that encourages students, space enthusiasts, and aspiring explorers to understand the exciting world of space exploration.

ORBITAL COMMAND AI — Design. Launch. Survive. Discover.
details:
ORBITAL COMMAND AI – Design. Launch. Survive. Discover.

What does it do and how does it work?

ORBITAL COMMAND AI is an interactive space mission design and simulation platform that makes exploring space mission concepts more engaging and accessible.

Designing a space mission involves many interconnected decisions. Our platform brings important mission-planning activities together in one interactive environment. Users can explore mission objectives, configure spacecraft, select launch vehicles, manage mission resources, and experience space through interactive 3D visualizations and launch simulations.

The platform combines a mission-control-style interface with 3D space experiences to help users explore different aspects of space mission design.

What benefits does it have?

  • Makes complex space mission concepts easier to explore.
  • Provides an interactive environment for learning about mission planning.
  • Introduces users to spacecraft configuration and rocket selection.
  • Encourages experimentation and curiosity about space science.
  • Combines mission-related concepts with immersive 3D visualization.

What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to make space mission design more accessible, especially for students, beginners, and people interested in space exploration.

We want to encourage STEM education, promote interest in aerospace engineering, and help users understand that successful space missions require careful consideration of multiple interconnected factors.

ORBITAL COMMAND AI aims to turn abstract space mission concepts into an engaging, interactive learning experience.

Tools, coding languages, hardware, and software used

We developed the project as a web-based application using:

  • React – Building the interactive user interface.
  • JavaScript – Implementing application functionality and interactions.
  • Vite – Development and build tooling.
  • Three.js – Creating 3D space visualizations.
  • React Three Fiber – Integrating 3D graphics into React.
  • Drei – Supporting 3D scene development.
  • CSS – Styling and responsive layouts.
  • Git and GitHub – Version control and source code management.
  • Vercel – Hosting and deploying the web application.

The project was developed using standard computer hardware and software development tools.

How is the project creative and innovative?

Our creative approach is to bring mission planning and immersive 3D space visualization together in a single interactive platform.

Instead of presenting space mission concepts only through static explanations, ORBITAL COMMAND AI provides a mission-control-inspired experience where users can explore spacecraft, rockets, planetary environments, and mission scenarios.

The combination of an interactive dashboard, spacecraft configuration, resource considerations, and 3D visualization creates an engaging way to explore the complexity of space exploration.

What factors did our team consider?

Our team considered several important factors involved in space mission design:

  • Mission objectives and scientific goals.
  • Spacecraft configuration and payload considerations.
  • Rocket and launch vehicle selection.
  • Fuel, power, and resource requirements.
  • Communication and mission constraints.
  • User experience and accessibility.
  • Interactive visualization and learning value.
  • The importance of presenting mission concepts in an understandable way.

We also considered how to make the platform visually engaging while keeping the interface understandable for students and beginners.

Our Vision

We aim to continue developing ORBITAL COMMAND AI with more realistic mission calculations, advanced orbital mechanics, spacecraft and propulsion modelling, additional planetary environments, NASA open-data integrations, and AI-assisted mission decision support.

ORBITAL COMMAND AI — Design. Launch. Survive. Discover.
